land.text: the coast 'between Brebes and Indramayu', a principality within Sunda from 1445-1447 that Sunda 'has lost control of' by 1513

predecessors.note: Cirebon was 'still a principality within the Sunda Kingdom' c. 1447 under Prince Cakrabuana and sent tribute to the Sunda court; Sharif Hidayatullah declared independence on 2 April 1482 (Sunda Kingdom page). The Cirebon infobox dates independence to 1479.

land.text: the Kasepuhan line of Muhammad Samsudin (1677-1703)

successors.note: Cirebon page: Girilaya's three sons divided the sultanate in 1677 (formally with Kanoman in 1679). The Banten page has Tirtayasa crowning the Kasepuhan and Kanoman sultans at Banten in 1677.

land.text: the Kanoman line of Muhammad Badruddin (1677-1723)

capitals.name: Cirebon
capitals.note: The page names Cirebon as the town (Caruban, founded 1445-1447) and no other capital; city-centre coordinates.

rulers.note: succeeded Prince Cakrabuana (1447-1479) in 1479; the 1479 date is the page's, its text puts the independence declaration at 1482; reviewer se-02-d: clipped to the state's start (2 April 1482); the infobox has his reign from 1479

region.text: the coast 'between Brebes and Indramayu' round Cirebon

ledger.note: 2 April 1482: Sunan Gunungjati stops Cirebon's tribute to Pajajaran. 'On 2 April 1482, Sunan Gunungjati stated that Cirebon will no longer send tribute to Pajajaran' ('By 1482 ... Cirebon declared its independence from Sunda'). The Cirebon infobox gives 1479; the settlement dates from 1445.

region.text: Banten, conquered by Syarif Hidayatullah's son Hasanuddin ('De jure province of Cirebon Sultanate (1526-1552)')

ledger.note: 1526: Banten conquered; its king Hasanuddin is Cirebon's vassal under Demak's auspices (infobox 'Syarif Hidayatullah conquered Banten: 1526'; the Sunda Kingdom page: 'Sunan Gunungjati of Cirebon later crowned his son, Hasanuddin, as the king of Banten'). The Banten page says Old Banten became a province under Cirebon in 1531.
1552: Banten becomes independent of Cirebon (infobox 'Independence from Cirebon Sultanate: 1552').

region.text: the Cirebon coast, divided among Girilaya's three sons

ledger.note: 1677: Cirebon is partitioned. 'Panembahan Girilaya's three sons divided the sultanate': Muhammad Samsudin ruled Kasepuhan (1677-1703), Muhammad Badruddin ruled Kanoman (1677-1723), Nasruddin ruled Keprabonan (1677-1713); Kasepuhan and Kanoman were formally divided in 1679.
1677: the Kanoman share goes to Muhammad Badruddin.
1677: the Keprabonan share goes to Nasruddin.

1677: the sultanate of Cirebon ends in the three-way partition. Banten had the princes crowned at Banten (Banten page); the Dutch and Mataram then forced Banten to give up Cirebon in the late 1670s, and under Amangkurat II 'Cirebon too was forced to shift allegiance from Mataram to the Dutch' (Mataram page; 'In 1705 he agreed to cede the regions of Cirebon' to the VOC).

wars.name: Cirebon-Demak war on Sunda

zones.text: Sunda Kalapa, the harbour taken by Fatahillah in 1527

wars.outcome: Banten (1526) and Sunda Kalapa (1527, renamed Jayakarta) taken by Cirebon-Demak forces; King Surawisesa of Sunda made peace with Cirebon in 1531.
wars.note: 'in 1527 Fatahillah, a military commander sent from Demak, managed to capture the Sunda Kalapa harbour just before the Portuguese returned'; 'The army of Fatahillah, comprising around Cirebon-Demak troops'; 'In 1531 ... a peace treaty was concluded between King Surawisesa of Sunda and Syarif Hidayatullah of Cirebon'. The Banten page adds that Demak and Cirebon beat a Portuguese fleet in 1527.

wars.name: Cirebon's suppression of the Sumedang and Ciamis rebellions
wars.outcome: Cirebon, asked by Sultan Agung to help against Batavia, defeated the Sumedang and Ciamis rebellions in 1618 and 1619; no land passed to Cirebon.
wars.note: The page says Cirebon was under Mataram's influence, though officially sovereign.

wars.name: Pagarage (Pacirebonan) war
wars.outcome: Banten's navy beat Mataram's about sixty ships with Cirebonese troops off Tanara; no land changed hands.
wars.note: Banten page: 'This war is known as Pagarage war or Pacirebonan war that took place in 1650.' The Cirebon page: 'Cirebon sent 60 ships against Banten's port ... and suffered a disastrous defeat.'

wars.name: Banten's hold on Cirebon and its loss
wars.outcome: Tirtayasa installed the Cirebon princes at Banten in 1677; the Dutch allied with Mataram and fought Banten 'for two years', forcing it to give up control of Cirebon; Cirebon then passed from Mataram to the Dutch as a protectorate.
wars.note: The years of the Dutch-Banten fighting are not on the page ('Late 1670s'); the Mataram page puts the shift of allegiance under Amangkurat II (1680 on). Reviewer se-02-d: clipped to the dossier's end (1677); the fighting of the late 1670s belongs to the successor sultanates' years.

certainty.note: A coastal principality whose reach is a stretch of coast and a handful of vassal claims; no treaty line is dated by the pages opened.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Sultanate of Cirebon' 1482-1676: the 1579-1618, 1619-1672 and 1673-1676 shapes are the Cirebon core plus exactly the 83 cells of Cliopatria's last Sunda Kingdom shape (1578); the Sunda page gives that land to Banten (and the regalia to Sumedang Larang), not to Cirebon, so all three are adjusted to the core. Cirebon is a coastal principality, not a power over West Java.
Dates: independence 1479 (infobox) or 1482 (text, 2 April 1482); the dossier starts at 2 April 1482. The settlement dates from 1445 (page) and the prince Cakrabuana ruled it 1447-1479 as part of Sunda, outside this dossier's life. The Cirebon page's ruler list (Fatahillah 1568-1570 interlude) is used as given.
Vassal relations to other dossiers: Cirebon was forced to acknowledge Mataram's overlordship in 1595 (Mataram page: Senapati forced 'Cirebon and Galuh ... in 1595'), nominal sovereign but under Mataram's influence from 1613/1617-1619, married into Sultan Agung's house in 1625, a Dutch protectorate after Amangkurat II (1680 on) and ceded to the VOC in 1705. These tints belong in the Mataram dossier (mataram-sultanate: vassal_start 1595, vassal_end c. 1680) and the Dutch ones; Banten's page also makes Banten 'a de jure province of Cirebon 1526-1552' (recorded here as a vassal).
The successors Kasepuhan, Kanoman and Keprabonan have no Cliopatria row; they continue as protectorates and later (Kacirebonan 1807) as ceremonial courts. Slugs are my suggestions for dossiers (se-02-x or se-03).
Unresolved: the Sunda Kalapa conquest of 1527 is joint with Demak (Fatahillah was sent from Demak); I record it in the war entry and leave the gain to the Demak dossier because the town did not become Cirebon's direct land (it went to Banten). Pages not found: none; Cirebon page did not carry the VOC treaties of 1681 and 1705 (the Mataram page gives 1705).
